about:
# JustAC - Just Assisted Combat

A World of Warcraft addon that displays Blizzard's Assisted Combat spell suggestions with your keybinds, making it easier to follow the rotation helper without hunting for buttons.

## Features

### Where it shows

- **Main Queue** - a draggable panel: icon count, size, spacing and direction are yours to set, and it can dock to the target frame.
- **Nameplate Queue** - the same queue attached to your target's nameplate, with its own settings. Falls back to the main queue when the nameplate isn't on screen.
- Run either or both. Each has a **Show in** setting for the content it appears in (open world, delves and scenarios, dungeons, raids, PvP), so you can keep the queue for dungeons and hide it in raids.
- **Resource bar** (optional, per surface) - your primary power plus a segmented bar for combo points, runes, chi, holy power, soul shards or essence.

### Damage queue

- The **first slot** is the game's own Assisted Combat pick, with your keybind. A spell you've hidden is replaced by the next one the game would suggest.
- The **queue** after it is ordered by the **Priority** you choose - the game's order, the theorycraft (SimulationCraft) order, or your own list - and re-ranked for the fight in front of you: area abilities rise for a pack, abilities you can't use right now (out of range, wrong form, not in stealth, missing their proc) drop to the back, and procs come first.
- **DoT awareness** - a damage-over-time effect already on your target steps back until it's time to refresh. When the game keeps recommending one that's already up, an arrow on the first slot suggests spreading it to another enemy.
- **Burst-ready cue** - your major cooldown glows orange when a burst window is actually called for, not merely when it's off cooldown, and moves up to the second slot. Trigger lists come from SimulationCraft per spec and can be edited under DPS Queue → Burst.
- **Gap-closers** - melee specs get a blue movement cue when the target is out of range (DPS Queue → Gap-Closers).
- **Mana Conservation** (both clients, off by default; tune Forever first) - under DPS Queue → General → Queue Content, choose Solo Only or Always (PvE). With one detected normal enemy and safe player health, an available free attack can lead ahead of a mana-costing single-target attack, including the game's recommendation, when mana is low or recovery would be slow. Multiple detected enemies or recent cleave/AoE context block conservation. Prefers confirmed reach; unknown/out-of-range attacks can still lead, leaving positioning to you. No level cutoff; custom/exact lists, procs and utility picks remain unchanged.
- **On the Move** - while you keep moving in combat, attacks you can cast on the move rise ahead of spells that need you to stand still. On by default for ranged and healers (DPS Queue → General → Queue Content).
- **Prioritize Your Own Targets** *(off by default)* - on an enemy that isn't attacking you, long cooldowns and burst wait for one you get credit for; on another player's enemy, damage over time waits too. Openers are never held.
- **Ability markers** - a dot marks abilities you can cast while moving, and (optionally) abilities that don't trigger the global cooldown.
- Spells, trinkets and on-use items are all supported. Icons grey out during casts and channels so you can see what's next.

### Glow colors

Native proc and Assisted Combat art stay unchanged. Custom tints use WoW-like
activity colors, rather than class or spell-school colors:

| Color | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Native gold | Proc or emergency-ready cast |
| Native blue-white | Primary Assisted Combat recommendation |
| Green | Defensive/healing recommendation |
| Azure blue | Movement/gap-closer |
| White | Crowd-control escape |
| Soft blue | Tank mitigation upkeep |
| Red | Interrupt/stop an enemy cast |
| Cyan | Cleanse an enemy enrage |
| Orange | Offensive burst window or execute |
| Violet | Buff/enchantment preparation |
| Magenta | Threat button (Forever, opt-in): drop threat, taunt or hold aggro |

Preparation and mitigation keep the same hue when their reminder ring escalates
to a proc-style glow. Existing glow controls and recommendation priorities still
apply; color alone is not a claim that a spell has procced.

### Priority

**Mana Conservation** offers only Off, Solo Only and Always (PvE), with no
percentage or recovery-time tuning controls. Existing saved tuning is preserved.
The option greys out when
the player is confirmed to have no mana pool. Hybrid forms are checked against
explicit mana capacity, not their current energy/rage bar. Saved settings are
preserved; unreadable capacity is not treated as absence. This is a mana policy,
not a reserve rule for energy, focus, rage, runic power or discrete resources.

Mana Conservation displays **WAIT** instead of another auto-attack prompt when the
attack is confirmed running and in range, unless another eligible in-range free
attack needs starting. Unknown running state or reach keeps the attack prompt.
Shoot requires a wand equipped; other ranged auto-attacks likewise require a
compatible weapon. Swapping equipment refreshes the available attacks.
Before pulling, automatic queues without a native game pick keep a ready attack
ahead of DPS buffs even when out of range, as a cue to move closer. Combat
range ordering and custom/exact lists are unchanged.

On Forever, automatic filler weighs a free wand or an in-reach melee attack
against your casts. While you have mana to spare, a supported cast leads whenever
its estimated damage per second is ahead. Once mana runs low in a fight, the free
attack is favored for the rest of that fight until a cast offers at least 20% more.
The comparison uses readable pre-combat stats and observed cast pushback, and
learns from the game's damage meter after each fight how much your weapons and
your casts really deal (talents, crits and misses included; damage over time from
fights against one enemy), so a new weapon or a higher weapon skill shows up
within a few fights. The opening press and the attack used against an enemy that
keeps its distance are ordered by the same measured damage. Unknown estimates
and custom/exact ordering retain their usual behavior.

- **Three orders, one queue** - tabs show the game's order, the theorycraft order and your own list, one line per ability with what it waits for. Looking at a tab never changes the queue; **Use This Order** does, and a green dot marks the one in use.
- **Your own list** (per spec) - start from **Export to My List** or **Merge** from another tab, then drag rows to reorder. Click a row for its settings, right-click to open it on the Overrides tab, and undo the last ten changes. If the game's rotation changes later, **Merge Changes** brings your list up to date without reordering it.
- **Who leads** - the first slot is the game's by default. **Fill the gaps** lets the queue use it only while the game has nothing to recommend; **Replace with my list** gives it to your list's first ready entry.
- **Ordering** - Procs first, Unavailable last, and **Use my order exactly** to turn off re-ranking for the fight.
- Per ability: **Always Show** keeps it from being filtered out, and **Hold Until** parks it at the back until it's fully charged.
- Talent variants of the same ability are recognised, so a list survives a talent swap.
- **`/jac why <spell>`** explains why an ability is or isn't showing right now.

### Disruption slot

The slot ahead of the damage queue, for anything that stops what the enemy is doing. Each part can be turned on or off on its own.

- **Interrupts** when your target is casting, optionally only for casts the game marks as important. Hidden on casts that can't be interrupted.
- **Crowd control** on unimportant casts, saving your interrupt for dangerous ones. Knows which crowd control works on which creature type, and which targets are immune.
- **Enrage cleanses** - when an enemy enrages and you carry a dispel for it (Soothe, Tranquilizing Shot, Shiv and the like), it shows here with a cyan glow.
- Works with the default nameplates and with nameplate addons that keep a compatible cast bar.

### Defensives

- **Your defensive list** - self-heals and major cooldowns in one list with per-spec defaults, arranged the same way as the damage priority. Pet rez/summon and pet heal have lists of their own.
- Pet summon and revive reminders appear on the pre-combat queue without duplicating damage suggestions. Beast Mastery Hunters and Demonology Warlocks can also receive reminders during combat.
- **Help Your Group** - party-wide buttons (Rallying Cry, Darkness, Anti-Magic Zone, Vampiric Embrace and the like) in a list of their own, offered when your group could use the help or your own health is low.
- **Emergency heals held until you need them** *(on by default)* - immunity bubbles, big instant heals and health potions wait at the end of the queue with a WAIT tag while you're healthy. Damage-reduction cooldowns stay live, since a wall is meant to be pressed before the hit lands.
- The order follows how much trouble you're in: damage reduction first while you're taking damage, big heals after a real hit, bubbles only when you're close to dying.
- **Best healing potion** - picks the potion you're carrying that heals you most.
- Absorb shields step back while their barrier holds, instead of being suggested into a wasted overwrite.
- Druid defensives that need Bear or Cat Form only show in that form (unless you have Fluid Form).
- Compact health bar for you and your pet.

#### Sustain slot

Ahead of the defensives, for what keeps you contributing rather than what keeps you alive:

- **Tank maintenance** - your spec's mitigation buff (Ignore Pain, Shield of the Righteous, Ironfur, Demon Spikes, Bone Shield) with its time left, a warning ring before it drops and a full glow once it has. Set how early it warns, add an alert sound, and have charge-based buffs glow while every charge is ready. Brewmaster isn't covered yet. Most accurate with the Cooldown Manager's **Tracked Bars** left visible in Edit Mode.
- **Crowd Control Escape** *(experimental, opt-in)* - while you're stunned, rooted or feared and have something ready to break it, the slot shows that button.
- **Pet heal** - Hunters are reminded when their pet is low, in combat too.

### Healers

JustAC isn't a healing addon - keep yours. It covers the other half of the job:

- **Damage priority with your heals filtered out**, so the time between heals still does damage. Every healer spec has its own damage priority.
- **Caster mode** *(per spec, opt-in)* - no melee-range or form-shift suggestions for healers who stay at range.
- **Group heal suggestions** - area heals when several allies are hurt, and your biggest save (Tranquility, Aura Mastery, Healing Tide, Divine Hymn, Restoral, Rewind) when the group is in serious trouble.

### Preparation

The Preparation tab groups Between-pull Recovery, Buffs & Enhancements, and
class-appropriate Combat Readiness. Health Recovery Below controls self-heal spells, not
recovery food. Food Buff chooses food for its buff. Health Recovery defaults to
Auto: when you're hurt it prefers a ready, usable short-cooldown self-heal, then
food or a bandage. Choose a learned heal to prefer it, or Food / Bandage for
item recovery. Mana Recovery Items stays independent; both selectors inherit the old
Recovery setting until explicitly changed. Combined food/drink qualifies for
either enabled need and appears once, including when also suggested for its buff.

- Out of combat, the defensive queue shows buffs you're **missing but own** - flask, food, augment rune, weapon enchant, poisons, shields, imbues and the group buffs - as icons you can click to use.
- On Forever, a missing Paladin seal also appears in pre-combat preparation. Out of combat, timed preparation buffs are offered again once they could run out during your next fight, only with readable timing and a ready, usable cooldown-free spell. Refresh preserves the active buff choice; permanent effects, forms and unreadable timers stay quiet. Combat remains missing-only.
- Preparation and recovery heals appear before consumables on the pre-combat bar, without duplicating DPS slot 1. Hidden or disabled preparation leaves the DPS fallback available.
- Missing critical preparation and safe OOC refreshes get animated violet emphasis with a live hostile targeted, including in Proc Only mode. Genuine gold procs retain precedence.
- Forever also prepares Protection's Righteous Fury, Shadowform, Balance's Moonkin Form and Battle Shout when usable; missing stances follow the installed tree, and Survival Hunters default to Aspect of the Beast when no aspect is active. Retail includes specialization-appropriate Druid forms, Shadowform and Paladin weapon rites.
- Form reminders never replace an active form or ask you to shift while mounted. Existing weapon enchants satisfy rite preparation without being overwritten.
- Group buffs are offered again when a party member is missing one, so one cast covers everyone.
- **Recuperate** *(opt-in)* - offered when you're below your top-off level out of combat.
- The reminder needs confirmed missing health and stays quiet when that cannot be read. Critical-health reminders remain separate.
- **Forever mana recovery** - with Mana Recovery Items on Auto, offers your best owned, usable drink when your mana is low. Requires confirmed low mana and stops while eating or drinking. Health Recovery saves food and bandages when a suitable self-heal is usable or already healing you.
- Covers every expansion's consumables, so leveling characters are covered too, and weapon enchants match the weapon you have equipped.

### Keybinds and filtering

- Finds your keybind for every suggestion across all action bars, including macros with conditions (`[mod]`, `[form]`, `[spec]`, `[stealth]`, `[combat]`) and transformed spells. Gamepad button icons for Xbox, PlayStation and generic controllers.
- Ability search filters out unlearned, off-spec and passive spells, and refreshes pet abilities when your pet changes.
- Right-click an icon to set your own hotkey label; icons flash when you press their key.
- Buffs you already have, your current form and a pet that's already out aren't suggested. Abilities that stack keep being suggested while you build stacks.
- **Overrides** tab - hide a spell (or Shift+Right-click it in the queue), change its queue settings, or **take it off your action bars** so the game's assist stops suggesting it too. **Put Back** restores it to the same buttons; macros are never touched.
- Light on your CPU: event-driven, with other players' events filtered out before they reach the addon.

## WoW Forever

JustAC supports Retail and WoW Forever from the same download. The addon is no longer a beta release; the Forever client is still in beta, and the in-game testing caveats below still apply.

WoW Forever has no Assisted Combat, so JustAC builds the queue itself. The first slot is JustAC's own pick rather than the game's, and the order comes from a priority for every class and talent tree (from the Forever simulations, tuned for levelling). The queue suggests only what that priority uses, plus your weapon attacks (Attack, Auto Shot, wand, Throw); anything it leaves out, such as forms and self buffs, stays with you, and Charge and Intercept come from Gap-Closer Suggestions. Macros and abilities without bindings are included; action-bar ranks are preferred. Throw or a ranged weapon can lead while your melee attacks are out of reach.

These are general-purpose priorities, intended to be useful in most ordinary fights, not optimal in every situation. Specialized simulator sequences and seal twisting are not part of the defaults. Conditions use the client signals JustAC can reliably check; unavailable information is not guessed. Your custom priority list and explicit settings remain your choice.

What works differently on Forever:

- **Play Style** *(WoW Forever section of the options)* - which talent tree's priority the queue follows. Automatic follows your talent points, but skips a tree whose attacks need gear you are not wearing (Protection without a shield, for example), and druids follow their caster or bear priority by form. The section shows which priority is in use and why.
- **Spell ranks** - the queue shows the rank you have on your bars, with its keybind, and finds any rank in your lists.
- **WAIT** - with Unavailable Last and ranked ordering, the timer icon leads when every DPS ability is unavailable. The waiting abilities stay behind it, and an eligible suggestion replaces it. Out of combat this requires a live enemy you can attack; no-target previews are unchanged.
- **Save burst for worthwhile fights** - automatic priorities reserve confirmed self-buffs with a base cooldown of at least two minutes until an elite, boss or multiple engaged enemies are confirmed. The reservation persists before and after combat and through missing encounter information; unknown spell classification or cooldown does not qualify a spell for reservation. Custom lists, Always Show, explicit Hold Until settings and custom burst triggers retain control. With no other eligible ability, WAIT leads instead of spending the cooldown.
- **Between ranged shots** - while the enemy is confirmed beyond melee reach, an otherwise eligible Throw or ranged weapon filler keeps its first slot and cooldown swipe instead of alternating with WAIT. Any ready alternative takes precedence; blocked or unknown shot range still falls back to WAIT.
- **Rear-required attacks** - Backstab, Shred and similar attacks are left out of the queue while you are out of stealth and the enemy is targeting you, or has no target yet (it turns to face you with the first hit). They are offered in stealth or once the enemy turns to someone else (a tank or a pet). This is a targeting rule, not a facing check (the game gives no way to read facing); unreadable targeting information leaves them in, and turning off Unavailable Last keeps them in their place.
- **Tiered damage finishers** - on normal enemies, aim for fewer combo points as the enemy weakens, and the minimum needed near death. Bosses and elites retain the imported point target. Fixed-cost spenders and duration-based finishers keep their own requirements.
- **Swing timers** - Heroic Strike, Cleave, Raptor Strike and Maul show a bar filling to the swing they wait for, and a tick in place of the keybind while pressing again would do nothing. Attack, Auto Shot and wands show their swing timer while they run.
- **Auto Shot and Attack** trade places as you move in and out of melee range.
- **Damage over time** is timed from your own casts, including your opener: it steps back while it ticks, comes back as it runs out, and isn't suggested on a target about to die. Solo against one ordinary enemy at or below your level, it is only offered early in the fight. Tracking it in the Cooldown Manager makes this exact.
- **Resource presses** - Life Tap, Evocation and Innervate come forward when you can't afford your spells; Life Tap, Bloodrage and Hellfire only while your health is above half.
- **Area abilities** lead when two or more enemies are fighting you; pack attacks such as Thunder Clap lead from three.
- **Shared resources** - a cheaper ability never spends the rage, energy or mana a higher-priority one is waiting for, and while everything waits the first slot shows what comes next.
- **Threat Button** *(opt-in, Defensives)* - in a group or with your pet out, a magenta button in the interrupt button's spot (an interrupt takes it first), hidden until threat needs a press: a threat drop when you are about to pull aggro, or a taunt or threat ability when you are tanking and losing it.
- **Between pulls** - food, drink or a bandage when you need them, and the flasks, elixirs and scrolls you carry (Defensive Queue → Pre-Combat Buffs).
- Options that only apply to Assisted Combat are greyed out.

Interrupt cues require an attackable target, so friendly players' casts do not trigger them.

Still being checked in game: the rear-attack targeting heuristic, WAIT transitions, crowd-control escape and interrupt cues, and lists past the beta's level cap.

## Installation

1. Download from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/just-assisted-combat) or extract to `Interface\AddOns\JustAC`
2. Retail: enable "Assisted Combat" in WoW's Game Menu → Edit Mode → Combat section (WoW Forever has none - nothing to enable)
3. `/jac` to access options

## Configuration

Options are organized into 6 tabs, plus a seventh on WoW Forever:

| Tab | Purpose |
|-----|--------|
| **General** | Disruption slot (interrupts, enrage cleanse, dangerous-cast warning), input, Blizzard UI integration (action-bar highlight, Cooldown Manager) |
| **Display** | 3 sub-tabs: Main Queue (the draggable surface: layout/docking, DPS icons, defensive icons, appearance), Nameplate Queue (the nameplate surface), and Shared Behavior (highlight mode, ability markers, icon labels) |
| **DPS Queue** | Priority (the game's order, the theorycraft order, or your own list, and who leads), ordering, queue content, burst triggers and cue, gap-closers |
| **Defensive Queue** | 2 sub-tabs: General (the priority lists, Help Your Group, ordering, Sustain slot: tank maintenance, CC escape, pet heal), Pre-Combat Buffs |
| **Overrides** | Everything set on one spell or item: visibility (the blacklist) and taking it off your action bars, queue and item settings, situational sets, hotkey label. Lists everything you've customized; click an entry to open its settings under it |
| **Profiles** | AceDB profiles with automatic per-spec switching |
| **WoW Forever** | Shown only on WoW Forever: Play Style (which talent tree's priority the queue follows, and why) and tracking your rotation's buffs in the Cooldown Manager |

- **Localization** - English, German, French, Italian, Russian, Spanish (ES/MX), Portuguese (BR), Korean, Simplified/Traditional Chinese

[MythicSim Forever engine](https://github.com/sage3648/mythicsim-forever-engine),
pinned to the revision recorded in `tools/forever-apl-src/UPSTREAM_COMMIT`.
The mirror's `presets/catalog.json` records its application-data source revision.
JustAC maps the lists to supported secret-safe gates, filters spells by Forever
learnability, and retains local healer damage-filler pins. The original MIT
license and notice are vendored; generated rotations include the full MIT license.
Source revisions and adaptations are documented in
[CLIENT_COMPAT.md](https://github.com/wealdly/JustAC/blob/main/Documentation/CLIENT_COMPAT.md#forever-rotation-source-review).

### WoW Forever distance reference items

The four reference items JustAC uses to bracket target distance on WoW Forever
(Voodoo Charm and Curative Animal Salve at 5 yards, Treant and Wildkin Muisek
Vessels at 10 yards) and their yardages come from the Classic Era/Forever list in
[LibRangeCheck-3.0](https://github.com/WeakAuras/LibRangeCheck-3.0) by mitch0 and
The WoWUIDev Community (MIT license, revision `3f9e454`). The library is not
embedded. JustAC uses two items per distance, requires both to agree, and counts a
negative answer only for a live attackable target. See
[Data/RangeReferences.lua](https://github.com/wealdly/JustAC/blob/main/Data/RangeReferences.lua).

### Retail priority lists

Retail's alternate priorities derive from the
[SimulationCraft project and its contributors](https://github.com/simulationcraft/simc),
under GPL-3.0. JustAC adapts those lists to its supported combat-safe conditions
and retains local healer damage-filler lists. Source revisions and refresh
procedures are documented in
[DEV_TOOLING.md](https://github.com/wealdly/JustAC/blob/main/Documentation/DEV_TOOLING.md#two-client-update-check-and-refresh).

For the Combat Assistant system. The `C_AssistedCombat` API powers this entire addon-JustAC simply presents what Blizzard's system suggests in a more accessible format.

### The WoW Addon Community

To everyone who has contributed to wowace.com, curseforge, GitHub discussions, and the countless forum threads that help addon developers learn and grow. Your shared knowledge makes projects like this possible.

## Technical Notes

- **Midnight compliant, targeting Retail 12.1.5** - Built around the secret-value system rather than patched over it: `auraInstanceID` mapping for combat-safe buff detection, `isOnGCD` for cooldown readiness, opaque cooldown pipeline, NeverSecret aura whitelist, fail-open design throughout. `/jac inspect validate` self-tests each of these against a known-correct answer, so a patch that changes the rules reports itself instead of degrading quietly
- **Secret-safe visuals** - Where a combat state is a "secret value" that can't be read or branched on (e.g. cast interruptibility), it's forwarded straight into a display sink (`SetAlphaFromBoolean` / `SetCooldownFromDurationObject`) so the engine renders it without the addon ever seeing the value
- **Taint is fatal around secrets** - Tainted execution cannot read a secret at all, so writing any Lua field on a frame that reads secrets (Blizzard's Cooldown Manager viewers) breaks *Blizzard's* code, not just ours. Reads and widget C methods are safe; mixin methods that store state are not. See [AURA_IDENTITY_12.0.md](https://github.com/wealdly/JustAC/blob/main/Documentation/AURA_IDENTITY_12.0.md)
- **Never-secret signals** - Readable side-channels fill gaps where a value is secret: the low-health vignette, and player `UNIT_HEALTH` *event activity* - out-of-combat regen fires events while below full health and goes silent at full, so the firing itself is a "still recovering" signal even when the payload is secret
- **No External Spell Databases** - Native spell classification (`SpellDB` + generated `Data/` tables: archetypes, categories, base cooldowns & charges, aura stack counts, form/stealth requirements, caster-aura requirements, pure self-buffs, healing items, pre-combat buffs) replaces LibPlayerSpells; tables regenerate per patch from client data exports via `tools/`
- **Modular Architecture** - Lua modules across the `BlizzardAPI`, `UI`, `Options`, `Locales`, and `Data` subdirectories, plus library dependencies, with a clear load/dependency order
- **Event-Driven** - Minimal polling; push-based cooldown/range/usability events mark queues dirty for responsive updates
- **Cache-Smart** - Aggressive caching with proper invalidation (throttled, state-hash, event-driven, instance-scoped patterns)

## Commands

```text
/jac                          - Open options panel
/jac toggle                   - Pause/resume display
/jac debug                    - Toggle debug mode
/jac reset                    - Reset frame position
/jac profile [name|list]      - Switch or list profiles
/jac find [spell]             - Find spell on action bars (defaults to AC suggestion)
/jac why [spell]              - Explain stage by stage why an ability is or isn't showing
/jac hud                      - Toggle the diagnostic HUD
/jac help                     - Every command and inspect topic, with descriptions
```

`/jac inspect <topic>` covers dozens of diagnostics. The list isn't duplicated here - it
lives next to the code it inspects and `/jac help` prints it, so the two can't
drift apart. Three are worth knowing by name if something stops working, because
they separate "the game changed" from "the addon broke":

| Command | Answers |
|---|---|
| `/jac inspect validate` | Did a secrecy rule change, or did one of the techniques the addon relies on stop producing its known-correct answer? `arm` diffs across a combat enter/exit |
| `/jac inspect errors` | Did we start taking Lua errors or taint blocks? Run it after a fight |
| `/jac inspect secrecy` | Which combat values actually read plain vs. hidden, right where you're standing |

### [6.7.0] - 2026-11-24

#### WoW Forever: tanking

- Tanking in a group (assigned Tank, or in a tank stance or form with no role set): Sunder Armor moves ahead of your filler attacks until its stack is full, for threat and for your group's physical damage. Alone, the order is unchanged.
- Protection warriors: Shield Block is now part of your attack queue, pressed on cooldown, since its blocks give the rage and Revenge chances your attacks run on.
- Protection paladins: Holy Shield is now part of your attack queue, kept up, since its blocks return mana and deal damage.
- Threat button: as a tank with three or more enemies attacking others and your target in reach, it offers a group taunt such as Challenging Shout. A shaman in the Tank role gets Stoneclaw Totem, which turns nearby enemies onto the totem.
- Threat button: a taunt that pulls the enemy straight to you, such as Taunt, comes before Mocking Blow, and threat abilities go by how much threat they add, so Sunder Armor comes before Demoralizing Shout.
- Threat button: a press out of range now shows with a red hotkey instead of not showing, so you can close the distance.

#### WoW Forever: classes

- Marksmanship hunters: Sniper Shot leads Aimed Shot only while Rapid Killing's next-shot bonus is up, as the leveling guides play it; otherwise Aimed Shot comes first.
- Feral cat: Ferocious Bite now spends your combo points when Rip would not be worth starting, such as on a nearly dead enemy or in a short group fight, instead of building past five with Claw.
- Feral bear: Swipe fills on a single target until you learn Lacerate or Primal Bite.

### [6.4.1] - 2026-11-18

#### Forever: queue behavior

- Fights against two or more enemies now follow each talent tree's own priority order. Before, area and unclassified abilities (including the wand) could be shown ahead of your main attacks.
- When several enemies are on you and you look away for a moment, the queue keeps its multi-target order for up to four seconds instead of switching to single-target abilities. It follows newly detected enemies promptly and drops the old count when combat ends.
- An attack that is already switched on (Attack, Auto Shot, wand Shoot) no longer takes a place in the queue, since pressing it again would only switch it off. It comes back as soon as it stops. When it is your best attack, the first slot shows WAIT so you keep attacking.
- Heroic Strike, Cleave and Raptor Strike: once queued, the ability stays in the first slot with its swing timer until the swing lands, instead of being replaced by WAIT or dropping off the end of the queue. An ability you can press during that swing still comes first.

#### Forever: damage and heals over time

- Solo against a single ordinary enemy at or below your level, damage over time effects are now offered only early in the fight, when they still have time to do their damage. Tougher fights (elites, bosses, higher-level enemies, packs) are unchanged. Spells that are mostly an immediate hit, such as Fireball and Moonfire, are not affected.
- A damage over time effect you just applied is less often suggested again because some other attack was missed, parried or dodged at about the same moment.
- The queue now learns when a particular kind of enemy is immune to one of your damage over time spells, and stops suggesting the spell against that kind of enemy in later fights. A miss or a resist is not treated as immunity. With a pet or in a group, it confirms the result on two different enemies first. If the spell is later seen to work on that kind of enemy, it is suggested again; that requires tracking the spell in the Cooldown Manager.
- Priests: Devouring Plague is now tracked like your other damage over time spells, including through the Cooldown Manager when you track it there.

- Spells that hit and then burn (Fireball, Pyroblast, Holy Fire) are now weighed against your wand like other attack spells. Before, they always stayed ahead of the wand, even while an enemy was hitting you through every cast.

### [6.4.0] - 2026-11-17

#### Buffs
- Maintained buffs (group buffs, armors, shields, seals, shouts, poisons and weapon imbues) are offered for a refresh when they could run out during your next fight, rather than minutes early. Targeting a boss or an elite, or being in a group, counts as a longer fight, so the reminder comes earlier there. The damage queue follows the same timing, so a buff that will outlast the fight no longer asks for a recast mid-combat.

#### Damage queue
- Spells that only work on certain kinds of creature, such as Repentance, are no longer suggested against creatures they cannot affect.
- Forever: the damage queue is about damage in every talent build, tanks included. Utility spells such as Demoralizing Shout, Frost Nova and Vampiric Embrace are left for you to use when the situation calls for them.
- Forever: a higher-priority attack about to come off cooldown keeps its rage or energy. A cheaper attack waits if spending now would leave you short when the better one is ready, such as Heroic Strike before Thunder Clap in a pack.
- Forever: against an enemy that fights from range, such as a caster or an archer, a slowing attack like Frostbolt gives way to a stronger attack that does not slow, like Fireball, when you have it.

#### Forever: damage and heals over time
- Damage and heals over time with a cast time come back early enough that the new cast lands as the old one finishes, instead of after it has already dropped. Stacking effects such as Lacerate come back a little earlier still, so their stacks are not lost.
- Priorities that wait on how long your own damage over time has left now follow it, for example Feral's Ferocious Bite only while Rip has a few seconds to spare.
- Sunder Armor counts your own applications on the target, so it is no longer suggested again while yours is still up.

#### Forever: priority lists
- Protection warriors lead with Thunder Clap against three or more enemies and use it whenever it is ready, instead of waiting for its slow to wear off.
- Exorcism and Holy Wrath are suggested only against Demons and Undead. Retribution now uses Exorcism, and Holy Wrath against packs, when the target is one.
- Priorities that depend on a spell being fast to cast, for example after a proc that makes it instant, follow the spell's current cast time.
